proposed_from.topic: Corrected gap-sensitive welfare-budgeted honest-width envelope for the targeting gain in an adaptive contextual experiment. Fix delta in (0,1/4), the Hölder-margin class, a P-independent benchmark policy, and the participant-welfare budget. Define W_{T,delta}(rho) over all non-anticipating designs and all honest interval procedures. Determine the complete frontier up to constants with a procedure-free converse and an attaining adaptive design/interval; optimize fixed-gap and Hölder-local subclasses, retain the compulsory rho^(-1/2) obstruction, and derive rather than assume all other branches, feasibility boundaries, and flattening thresholds. Exact formulas remain answer-open. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: packed bumps suggest feasibility T^(1-p), oracle width T^(-q), and a fixed-gap rho^(-1/2) branch. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: a uniform budget-saturating exploration lemma. EARLY KILL TEST: the d=1,beta=1,alpha=1/5 Gaussian construction near rho=T^(3/5).

The second characterizes pointwise regularity and online inference for optimal value under a supplied design and a negligible rule-value remainder. PraharajKhamaru2025AvoidingPriceAdaptivity shows that one stable linear contextual-bandit algorithm can retain near-minimax regret and support asymptotic Wald inference for fixed linear functionals, but it does not address a nonsmooth targeting gain, uniform honest expected width, or a hard welfare budget. None of these results derives the Hölder-margin transition map for the scalar targeting gain.","why_not_subsumed":"Adaptive change of measure alone does not ensure that alternatives separate \\(\\theta(P)\\), and an optimal-value influence function alone does not control the tie remainder uniformly. It also contains a decisive falsification point: any proposed formula must work at \\(d=1\\), \\(\\beta=1\\), \\(\\alpha=1/5\\), and \\(\\rho\\asymp T^{3/5}\\).","adversarial_boundary":"A packed sign-symmetric contextual-bandit construction can have large classification regret separation but zero targeting-gain separation. seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Procedure-free fixed-gap converse joined to the unresolved Hölder-local width frontier.
seed_details.summary: Characterize the minimax expected length over every adaptive design and honest interval, derive all welfare-budget branches, and attain them with one design and interval.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction formulates participant regret against treatment-effect precision; Theorems 1, 2, 5, and 6 and their proofs derive and attain a product frontier through suboptimal-arm counts; the Conclusion leaves richer action models open, and the shrinking-gap discussion leaves an intermediate regime unmatched.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace estimator-risk separation by two-law simultaneous-coverage separation, then replace a global suboptimal-arm count by a context-local count whose price is the unknown treatment gap.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for honest expected width, optimal-value gain, contextual bandits, and welfare or regret budgets found fixed-policy intervals and regular efficiency results but no all-design width envelope.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Simchi-Levi and Wang because confidence width is just estimation error.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their objective fixes a point estimator and a finite-arm linear gap; uniform interval coverage for \(\tau_+\) requires target-separating local alternatives and remains meaningful when pointwise asymptotic variance does not.
seed_details.burned_reason: The selected complete-honest-width-frontier angle exhausted three D0 solve rounds; its proposed saturation/common-realization upgrade restated the unresolved kernel without a concrete proof route for the mandatory d=1, beta=1, alpha=1/5, rho proportional to T^(3/5) case.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Scalar-functional local modulus under endogenous arm-specific information.
seed_details.summary: Build sign-asymmetric Hölder-margin Gaussian mixtures that separate the targeting gain and characterize their adaptive ordered modulus.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction distinguishes optimal-rule learning from optimal-value inference; Theorem 1 proves pathwise differentiability exactly away from noisy ties, Theorem 2 controls an online one-step estimator through rule-value remainder conditions, and the Discussion records the asymmetry between lower and two-sided inference.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the assumed negligible value remainder by an explicit coverage-testing modulus and construct alternatives whose scalar positive-part integrals cannot cancel.
seed_details.destination_search: Han, Jiao, and Mukherjee provide polynomial and fuzzy-prior machinery for nonsmooth scalar functionals, while Perchet and Rigollet provide Hölder-margin bumps; no source combines either with adaptive arm-specific likelihood.
seed_details.red_team: The margin condition makes the optimal value regular, so Luedtke and van der Laan already imply the rate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem is pointwise and requires a remainder rate; union honesty along shrinking ties and endogenous exploration is exactly where that remainder is first order.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Uniform budget-saturating exploration and a connected attaining interval.
seed_details.summary: Learn continuous cheap-to-explore regions, saturate the welfare budget, and derive a uniform martingale limit with an explicit optimization-bias envelope.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction turns privacy-motivated participant welfare into an error--regret design problem; the ConSE theorem and proof learn finite context frequencies and balance second-stage trial lengths, while the lower proof uses Rademacher alternatives and adaptive KL; the concluding discussion retains finite contexts and fixed-order gaps.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace finite-stratum arrival counts by predictable local-polynomial confidence cells and prove a simultaneous lower bound on cellwise information and upper bound on gap-weighted welfare expenditure.
seed_details.destination_search: Hu, Kallus, and Mao supply selective smooth exploration, while Bibaut and coauthors supply variance stabilization; no located theorem derives both under a prescribed welfare budget.
seed_details.red_team: ConSE with a fine partition immediately handles continuous contexts.
seed_details.rebuttal: A fixed partition neither learns vanishing-gap geometry nor controls approximation bias, and its welfare price can be dominated by cells whose gap is estimated too late.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Efficiency bound for the regular fixed-gap edge under a welfare budget.
seed_details.summary: Derive the target-direction efficiency bound after optimizing predictable exploration under a fixed-gap welfare constraint and construct an attaining one-step interval.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction allows assignments based on covariates and past outcomes; the LAN theorem derives an all-design least-favorable information bound and the attaining section uses pilot-based Neyman allocation; the paper does not impose a welfare cost or shrinking positivity.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Add the gap-priced allocation constraint to the least-favorable information optimization before taking the LAN limit, instead of optimizing variance over unconstrained propensities.
seed_details.destination_search: Shen and coauthors now characterize directional-stability efficiency for regular scalar targets, which occupies much of the unconstrained stability lane but not the welfare-constrained design optimization.
seed_details.red_team: Armstrong's all-design efficiency theorem already permits adaptive assignments and therefore includes the budgeted subclass.
seed_details.rebuttal: Restriction to a budgeted subclass changes the attainable information set and its optimizer; nevertheless this seed is narrower than the full honest-width frontier and was not selected.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Choose a terminal policy while controlling participant welfare during learning.
seed_details.summary: Optimize terminal policy regret under a hard cumulative participant-welfare budget and derive an oracle inequality over Hölder-margin laws.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction poses contextual treatment choice; the ABSE theorem and proof balance bin refinement with successive elimination and the lower-bound discussion identifies the sharp Hölder-margin exponent; the conclusion emphasizes regret rather than uncertainty about the scalar gain.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Separate in-experiment welfare expenditure from terminal policy regret instead of using cumulative regret as the sole objective.
seed_details.destination_search: Adaptive policy-learning papers condition on diminishing exploration, and budgeted bandit papers optimize reward or resource constraints; the exact terminal-versus-participant frontier remains plausible but does not answer the stated interval question.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine constrained-regret restatement of contextual bandit theory.
seed_details.rebuttal: The two losses occur at different horizons and can yield a nontrivial allocation frontier, but the consumer is less direct than honest inference, so the seed was not selected.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: When do unweighted and variance-stabilized adaptive intervals agree under budgeted exploration?
seed_details.summary: Derive the observable target-direction information threshold at which an ordinary one-step interval and a stabilized adaptive interval share a limit law, and the shrinking-exploration side where they diverge.
seed_details.anchor_read: Armstrong's LAN construction identifies the optimal regular information bound, while the achieving designs rely on stable pilot estimates; its conclusion does not characterize failure under random, anisotropic information growth.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain the random predictable quadratic variation under welfare-driven shrinking propensities instead of replacing it by a deterministic positive-overlap limit.
seed_details.destination_search: Shen and coauthors establish directional stability in 2026 and verify LinUCB, making a generic stability frontier occupied; a novelty claim would need the nonsmooth targeting-gain direction and a budget-derived threshold.
seed_details.red_team: Directional stability already gives the exact equivalence condition.
seed_details.rebuttal: It settles regular targets under an imposed stability property but does not derive stability from a welfare budget; still, the overlap with that preprint lowers this seed's novelty rank.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Procedure-free fixed-gap honest-width lower bound with benchmark noncancellation.
seed_details.summary: Show that every honest interval has expected width at least order \(\rho^{-1/2}\) when the fixed benchmark places positive mass on the inferior arm, and match it with an adaptive interval.
seed_details.anchor_read: The product lower bound changes one suboptimal arm and converts its expected count into KL, while EXP3E supplies the matching count; the proof targets treatment-effect estimation error rather than simultaneous coverage.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Perturb the inferior regression while preserving the optimal policy, compute the induced change in the benchmark-relative gain, and invoke two-law coverage rather than estimator deviation.
seed_details.destination_search: Hadad and coauthors explicitly leave optimal worst-case confidence width open; no fixed-gap contextual honest-width result was located.
seed_details.red_team: The result is only Simchi-Levi and Wang with an interval wrapped around their estimator.
seed_details.rebuttal: The lower bound quantifies over all interval centers and needs benchmark-sensitive target separation, while the upper bound must be uniformly honest after adaptive sign learning.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Anytime-valid inference for an adaptively learned optimal-value gain.
seed_details.summary: Construct a confidence sequence for the targeting gain that remains valid under stopping and derive its width under Hölder-margin alternatives.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction separates policy optimization from off-policy evaluation; Theorem 1 builds a doubly robust betting confidence sequence by Ville's inequality for a fixed policy value; the Conclusion leaves uniform inference over a policy family open.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed target-policy pseudo-outcome by a lower envelope over learned policies and account for the positive-part optimization bias before applying a test supermartingale.
seed_details.destination_search: Ponomarev and Semenova give one-sided offline optimal-welfare bands, but no anytime two-sided gain interval was found.
seed_details.red_team: Uniformly unioning the fixed-policy confidence sequences immediately covers the optimizer.
seed_details.rebuttal: An uncountable smooth policy class and vanishing propensities make the union nonsharp, and the selected optimum changes the target; however anytime validity adds logarithmic overhead outside the fixed-horizon question, so the seed was not selected.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Finite-sample randomization inversion for the targeting gain.
seed_details.summary: Invert an assignment-orbit test to obtain a finite-sample interval for personalization gain under adaptive assignment.
seed_details.anchor_read: The paper obtains finite-sample coverage from predictable betting supermartingales, not assignment symmetry; its design-based remark conditions on potential outcomes but still targets a time-varying treatment contrast.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Find a group action preserving an adaptively generated assignment law while imputing the missing optimized potential outcomes.
seed_details.destination_search: Randomization-inference and conformal searches did not locate a nontrivial symmetry orbit for response-adaptive propensities and the weak-null optimal-value gain.
seed_details.red_team: Adaptive assignments are not exchangeable, so the required permutation group does not exist without conditioning away nearly all information.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the stated design class; this seed is dropped rather than padded into the retained set.

banked_reason: The promised complete Hölder–margin width frontier was replaced by an implicit one-sided occupation-relaxation lower bound: no explicit full-class branches or thresholds, and no law-independent attaining design and honest interval, are delivered.
banked_proposal_promise_gap: Accepted proposal promised the complete field-tier Hölder-margin frontier, all phase transitions, and an attaining law-independent adaptive design/connected honest interval; the result proved only the fixed-gap rho^-1/2 edge and a necessary baselinewise occupation lower relaxation, leaving the central explicit-rate, saturation, and realization claims open.
